svg.title: MBON11's response to 3-octanol holds like flies' only when its Kenyon cell synapses don't depress
svg.text: What ends MBON11's burst: the depression of its Kenyon cell synapses
Without it, MBON11's response to 3-octanol holds as flies' does (94 spikes/s from 0.5 to 1 s, flies 95-100; 132 evoked spikes, flies 118), though it peaks too high (224, flies 135-140).
Silencing APL doubles the Kenyon cells' firing but leaves the response brief. As tested the Kenyon cells keep firing, but the synapses their first spikes
depressed deliver 1.3% of the peak drive from 0.6 s on, where flies' EPSC keeps 43%.
